name: Pain de mie

steps.title: Check conditions before preparing
steps.text: At room temperatures of 25°C or above, use water chilled to about 5°C and reduce it by 10 g (mL).

steps.title: Prepare the pan and ingredients
steps.text: Fit the kneading blade firmly on the clean mounting shaft. Add only the initial bread-pan flour and other ingredients in a mound (exclude yeast, all dispenser additions and all ingredients reserved for later) in the centre of the bread pan; pour the water around the edges. Fit and lock the pan in the appliance. Put the yeast in the dry yeast dispenser. Close both lids securely. (Manual p. 18.)

steps.title: Set and start the machine
steps.text: Select program 1, then press Start. Do not open the lid after starting except at a documented manual-addition step.

steps.title: Remove and cool
steps.text: When the machine beeps at completion, press Cancel and unplug. Use dry oven mitts to remove the hot bread pan. Set it on a cloth-covered surface and cool for about 2 minutes, then remove the bread onto a raised wire rack. Check for the kneading blade before cutting. Do not use a knife, fork or chopsticks or touch the underside of the pan. (Manual pp. 18–19.)

notes: At room temperatures of 25°C or above, use water chilled to about 5°C and reduce it by 10 g (mL).
Timer availability is subject to the recipe ingredients and the restrictions on manual pp. 20 and 24; this companion does not choose a delayed start.
otherTime: Hands-on preparation: unspecified.

name: Melon bread (Custom bread)

steps.title: Check conditions before preparing
steps.text: Follow quantities exactly; excess dough can overflow and burn, producing smoke. The machine delay timer is unavailable for this program (manual pp. 8–11, 24).

steps.title: Make cookie dough
steps.text: Sift cake flour and baking powder. Cream room-temperature butter. Add sugar in 2–3 batches and beat pale and smooth. Add egg in 3–4 batches, reserving ½ teaspoon; add vanilla last. Fold in sifted ingredients until no dry flour. Form smooth disc, wrap, refrigerate at least 20 minutes (p. 39).

steps.title: Prepare bread pan
steps.text: Fit the kneading blade firmly on the clean mounting shaft. Add only the initial bread-pan flour and other ingredients in a mound (exclude yeast, all dispenser additions and all ingredients reserved for later) in the centre of the bread pan; pour the water around the edges. Fit and lock the pan in the appliance. Put the yeast in the dry yeast dispenser. Close both lids securely. (Manual p. 18.)

steps.title: Start
steps.text: Select program 17 and press Start.

steps.title: Roll cookie dough
steps.text: Roll to 14–15 cm circle between plastic wrap. Brush one side with reserved ½ teaspoon egg. Optional lattice marks must be no deeper than 1 mm.

steps.title: At machine beep, add topping
steps.text: Within 15 minutes: do not press Cancel. Centre bread dough; place cookie dough egg-side down. Press edges lightly, not hard; sprinkle granulated sugar. Close lid and press Start.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: When the machine beeps at completion, press Cancel and unplug. Use dry oven mitts to remove the hot bread pan. Set it on a cloth-covered surface and cool for about 2 minutes, then remove the bread onto a raised wire rack. Check for the kneading blade before cutting. Do not use a knife, fork or chopsticks or touch the underside of the pan. (Manual pp. 18–19.) Do not shake vigorously.

notes: Follow quantities exactly; excess dough can overflow and burn, producing smoke.
Manual work at 55 minutes after starting (p. 9). Program restarts automatically after 15 minutes.
The machine delay timer is unavailable for this program (manual pp. 8–11, 24).

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Fit kneading blade. Add egg-and-milk mixture, then yogurt, then remaining ingredients. Fit pan. At 15°C or below cut butter into 5 mm cubes.

steps.title: Start
steps.text: Select program 25 and press Start.

steps.title: Scrape flour at machine beep
steps.text: Open lid and scrape flour from sides using a rubber spatula; metal damages coating. Do not press Cancel. Within 3 minutes close lid and press Start again.

steps.title: Shape at next machine beep
steps.text: After about 1 minute(s), open lid, scrape dough from sides and shape into a dome. Do not press Cancel. Within 3 minutes close lid and press Start again.

steps.title: Finish and check
steps.text: At completion beeps press Cancel. Remove hot pan with dry oven mitts; cool about 2 minutes then remove gently. Check for blade. Vigorous shaking can damage shape. If underbaked, up to two additional baking cycles are available for about 15 minutes after completion, before interior cools. Select same program, set 1–20 minutes, press Start. If Cancel has not been pressed, set time then Start. Hold Cancel to stop.

notes: First scraping beep after about 2 minutes.
If 3 minutes elapse at scraping, the program resumes automatically.
If Cancel is pressed accidentally at an intervention, press Start within 10 minutes to resume (once only; pressing another key disables this).
The program resumes baking automatically after 3 minutes at the shaping step. Wipe oil fumes from lid and steam vent after use (pp. 86–87).

steps.title: Check conditions before preparing
steps.text: Do not soak rice; soaking makes mochi too soft. If accidentally soaked, suggested water reduction: 2 go 80 g (mL); 3 go 140 g (mL). The machine delay timer is unavailable for this program (manual pp. 8–11, 24).

steps.title: Rinse and drain
steps.text: Rinse rice until water runs clear. Do not soak. Drain in colander 30 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare and start
steps.text: Fit noodle/mochi blade. Add rice then water. Fit pan. Select program 36 and press Start.

steps.title: Open lid at machine beep
steps.text: At about 50 or 55 minutes (p. 10), open lid. Do not press Cancel. Leave lid open and press Start immediately to release excess moisture. If 30 minutes elapse pounding starts automatically with lid closed.

steps.title: Remove and shape
steps.text: Use dry oven mitts for the hot pan; do not touch hot parts (manual pp. 4–5). At completion beeps press Cancel. Remove pan immediately and cool until touchable (5–10 minutes). Lift mochi from underneath onto heat-resistant tray dusted with starch. Pinch and roll portions. Wet hands to eat immediately; starch hands for storage. Alternatively wrap directly in plastic wrap and cut into blocks.

steps.title: Store
steps.text: Cool and brush off excess starch. Keep in cool dry place up to 2 days, or double-bag sealed in freezer up to one month.

notes: Do not soak rice; soaking makes mochi too soft. If accidentally soaked, suggested water reduction: 2 go 80 g (mL); 3 go 140 g (mL).
Do not add hard ingredients such as beans; they can peel pan coating.
The machine delay timer is unavailable for this program (manual pp. 8–11, 24).

steps.title: Check conditions before preparing
steps.text: The machine delay timer is unavailable for this program (manual pp. 8–11, 24).

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Fit noodle/mochi blade. Mix flours (A) in bowl. Mix salt and lukewarm water (B) separately. Add A then B to pan.

steps.title: Start
steps.text: Select d7 with Dough key and press Start.

steps.title: Remove and rest
steps.text: At machine beeps press Cancel, remove dough immediately. Shape smooth-side-out ball, wrap to prevent drying. Rest about 2 hours at room temperature, in refrigerator if room warm.

steps.title: Roll and cut
steps.text: Divide into 2–4 equal pieces. Dust and roll from centre to 3 mm thickness. Bring refrigerated dough to room temperature first. Fold and cut into strips about 3 mm wide.

steps.title: Boil separately
steps.text: Bring plenty of water to boil in large saucepan. Shake off dusting flour and boil about 8–13 minutes. Rinse in cold water and drain.

notes: Soba and ramen dough cannot be made.
Storage: dust and wrap; refrigerate 2–3 days or cut into noodles, wrap and freeze about one month.
The machine delay timer is unavailable for this program (manual pp. 8–11, 24).

name: Cocoa butter cake

steps.title: Check conditions before preparing
steps.text: The machine delay timer is unavailable for this program (manual pp. 8–11, 24).

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Cut butter into 1 cm cubes and bring to room temperature. Fit kneading blade. Add butter, sugar, milk and egg in that order, then sifted cake flour and baking powder. Fit pan.

steps.title: Start
steps.text: Select program 28 and press Start.

steps.title: Scrape flour at machine beep
steps.text: At the machine beep, open the lid and scrape flour from the sides with a rubber spatula. Add the variation ingredient evenly now. Do not press Cancel. Within 15 minutes, close the lid and press Start again.

steps.title: Finish and check
steps.text: At completion beeps press Cancel. Remove hot pan with dry oven mitts; cool about 2 minutes then remove gently. Check for blade. Vigorous shaking can damage shape. If underbaked, up to two additional baking cycles are available for about 15 minutes after completion, before interior cools. Select same program, set 1–20 minutes, press Start. If Cancel has not been pressed, set time then Start. Hold Cancel to stop.

notes: Scrape flour after about 12 minutes (p. 10). Add solid extra ingredients evenly at the scraping step. Result resembles butter cake, not commercial sponge cake.
If 15 minutes elapse at scraping, the program resumes automatically.
If Cancel is pressed accidentally at an intervention, press Start within 10 minutes to resume (once only; pressing another key disables this).
Add solid ingredients evenly when scraping down flour.
The machine delay timer is unavailable for this program (manual pp. 8–11, 24).

name: Chocolate-chip butter cake

steps.title: Check conditions before preparing
steps.text: The machine delay timer is unavailable for this program (manual pp. 8–11, 24).

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Cut butter into 1 cm cubes and bring to room temperature. Fit kneading blade. Add butter, sugar, milk and egg in that order, then sifted cake flour and baking powder. Fit pan.

steps.title: Start
steps.text: Select program 28 and press Start.

steps.title: Scrape flour at machine beep
steps.text: At the machine beep, open the lid and scrape flour from the sides with a rubber spatula. Add the variation ingredient evenly now. Do not press Cancel. Within 15 minutes, close the lid and press Start again.

steps.title: Finish and check
steps.text: At completion beeps press Cancel. Remove hot pan with dry oven mitts; cool about 2 minutes then remove gently. Check for blade. Vigorous shaking can damage shape. If underbaked, up to two additional baking cycles are available for about 15 minutes after completion, before interior cools. Select same program, set 1–20 minutes, press Start. If Cancel has not been pressed, set time then Start. Hold Cancel to stop.

notes: Scrape flour after about 12 minutes (p. 10). Add solid extra ingredients evenly at the scraping step. Result resembles butter cake, not commercial sponge cake.
If 15 minutes elapse at scraping, the program resumes automatically.
If Cancel is pressed accidentally at an intervention, press Start within 10 minutes to resume (once only; pressing another key disables this).
Add solid ingredients evenly when scraping down flour.
The machine delay timer is unavailable for this program (manual pp. 8–11, 24).

name: Mugwort mochi (2 go)

ingredients.name: Dusting starch (potato starch, non-glutinous rice flour or cornstarch)

steps.title: Check conditions before preparing
steps.text: Do not soak rice; soaking makes mochi too soft. If accidentally soaked, suggested water reduction: 2 go 80 g (mL); 3 go 140 g (mL). The machine delay timer is unavailable for this program (manual pp. 8–11, 24).

steps.title: Rinse and drain
steps.text: Rinse rice until water runs clear. Do not soak. Drain in colander 30 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare and start
steps.text: Fit noodle/mochi blade. Add rice then water. Fit pan. Select program 36 and press Start.

steps.title: Open lid at machine beep
steps.text: At about 50 or 55 minutes (p. 10), open lid. Do not press Cancel. Leave lid open and press Start immediately to release excess moisture. If 30 minutes elapse pounding starts automatically with lid closed.

steps.title: Add during pounding
steps.text: Boil mugwort leaves, soak in cold water to remove bitterness, chop finely and squeeze well. Once pounding starts, gradually add the variation ingredients.

steps.title: Remove and shape
steps.text: Use dry oven mitts for the hot pan; do not touch hot parts (manual pp. 4–5). At completion beeps press Cancel. Remove pan immediately and cool until touchable (5–10 minutes). Lift mochi from underneath onto heat-resistant tray dusted with starch. Pinch and roll portions. Wet hands to eat immediately; starch hands for storage. Alternatively wrap directly in plastic wrap and cut into blocks.

steps.title: Store
steps.text: Cool and brush off excess starch. Keep in cool dry place up to 2 days, or double-bag sealed in freezer up to one month.

notes: Do not soak rice; soaking makes mochi too soft. If accidentally soaked, suggested water reduction: 2 go 80 g (mL); 3 go 140 g (mL).
Do not add hard ingredients such as beans; they can peel pan coating.
Boil mugwort leaves, soak in cold water to remove bitterness, chop finely and squeeze well.
The machine delay timer is unavailable for this program (manual pp. 8–11, 24).
otherTime: Drain 30 min before cycle; cool 5–10 min after cycle. Shaping time unspecified.

name: Double-chocolate pain de mie

steps.title: Check conditions and prepare reserved ingredients
steps.text: At room temperatures of 25°C or above, use water chilled to about 5°C and reduce the initial water by 10 g (mL).

steps.title: Prepare the pan
steps.text: Fit the kneading blade firmly on its clean shaft. Put only initial bread-pan ingredients in a mound at the centre; pour the initial liquid around the edges. Keep all reserved additions, fillings and toppings separate. Fit and lock the pan. Put the measured yeast in the dry yeast dispenser; close both lids.

steps.title: Set and start
steps.text: Select program 1. Set Raisin to “Yes ♪ / Normal mixing”. Press Start. Follow the machine display and beeps. Do not open the lid except at the documented addition step.

steps.title: Add at the Raisin beep
steps.text: At the machine’s Raisin addition beep, open the lid and add: Chocolate chips (freeze beforehand). Do not press Cancel. Close the lid and press Start within 3 minutes; the program resumes automatically after 3 minutes.

steps.title: Remove and cool
steps.text: When the machine beeps at completion, press Cancel and unplug. Use dry oven mitts to remove the hot bread pan. Set it on a cloth-covered surface and cool for about 2 minutes, then remove the bread onto a raised wire rack. Check for the kneading blade before cutting. Do not use a knife, fork or chopsticks or touch the underside of the pan. (Manual pp. 18–19.)

notes: At room temperatures of 25°C or above, use water chilled to about 5°C and reduce the initial water by 10 g (mL).

sourceText:
Program 11: French bread
Pain de campagne
(made with poolish)

Ingredients
900kcal

Poolish (pre-ferment)
<A>
Water (about 25°C) ... 100g(mL)
Dry yeast ... 0.7g(¼ small spoon)
Bread flour ... 100g

<B>
Bread flour ... 100g
Wholemeal flour ... 50g
Salt ... 5g(1 small spoon)
Cold water (5°C) * ... 90g(mL)

Dry yeast ... 1.4g(½ small spoon)

* At room temperatures of 25°C or
above, reduce the amount by 10 g
(mL).
Using a poolish takes a little more effort, but produces an authentic
pain de campagne. Do not use the delay timer when using a poolish.
For a simpler version, use the quantities given for the recipe without
poolish.

Without poolish (pre-ferment)

Bread flour ... 200g
Wholemeal flour ... 50g
Salt ... 5g(1 small spoon)
Cold water (5°C) * ... 190g(mL)
Dry yeast ... 1.4g(½ small spoon)

* At room temperatures of 25°C or
above, reduce the amount by 10 g
(mL).

Fit the kneading blade in the bread
pan and add all ingredients except
the dry yeast. Put the dry yeast in the
yeast dispenser. Select Program 11
and press Start.

Method

1 Make the poolish (pre-ferment)
① Put the water and dry yeast in a bowl and whisk to dissolve.
② Add the bread flour and mix with a rubber spatula until smooth,
with no dry flour remaining. The finished poolish should be 20–30°C.
③ Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a plastic bag. Leave at room
temperature for 60 minutes, then refrigerate for 8–18 hours.

2 Bake using Program 11
① Fit the kneading blade in the bread pan. Add B and the poolish A,
then place the pan in the machine.
② Put the dry yeast in the yeast dispenser, select Program 11 and press
Start.

3 Remove the loaf
Lay a towel underneath. Move your hands firmly downwards,
tapping against the work surface to release the bread. See
“French bread” in the instruction manual.

sourceText:
Method

1 Make the dough using Program 17
① Fit the kneading blade in the bread pan, add A, and place the
pan in the machine.
② Put the dry yeast in the yeast dispenser, select Program 17 and
press Start.
2 Remove the dough (finish the work within 15 minutes!)
① When the machine beeps, open the lid, remove the dough from the bread pan,
and remove the kneading blade.
• Do not press Cancel.
3 Roll out
① Roll the dough into a rectangle about
15 cm deep × 25 cm wide.
4 Shape
① Brush the nearest three-
quarters of the dough with milk.
Sprinkle with cinnamon sugar
and scatter over the dried fruit.
② Roll up from the edge nearest
you.
③ Cut into four equal lengths
and place in the bread pan.

5 Bake
(Press Start again.)

6 Make the icing
① Put B in a bowl and stir over a 60°C water bath to make the icing.

7 Finish
① When baked, remove the bread from the pan and drizzle with icing.

When making custom bread…

Keep the combined weight of dough and filling to
600 g or less!
• Too much filling may prevent the bread from
rising or baking through.
Avoid fillings with a high moisture content!
(Reduce their moisture by simmering, for
example, and let them cool to room
temperature.)
• They affect dough fermentation.

Prepare the filling in advance!
• You have 15 minutes to work.

steps.text: Fit the kneading blade firmly on its clean shaft. Put only initial bread-pan ingredients in a mound at the centre; pour the initial liquid around the edges. Keep all reserved additions, fillings and toppings separate. Fit and lock the pan. Put the measured yeast in the dry yeast dispenser; close both lids.

steps.title: Set and start
steps.text: Select program 22. Set Raisin to “Yes ♪ / Normal mixing”. Press Start. Follow the machine display and beeps. Do not open the lid except at the documented addition step.

steps.title: Add at the Raisin beep
steps.text: At the machine’s Raisin addition beep, open the lid and add: Lemon peel. Do not press Cancel. Close the lid and press Start within 3 minutes; the program resumes automatically after 3 minutes.

steps.title: Remove and cool
steps.text: When the machine beeps at completion, press Cancel and unplug. Use dry oven mitts to remove the hot bread pan. Set it on a cloth-covered surface and cool for about 2 minutes, then remove the bread onto a raised wire rack. Check for the kneading blade before cutting. Do not use a knife, fork or chopsticks or touch the underside of the pan. (Manual pp. 18–19.)

Weigh the prepared vegetable and egg, then add soy milk according to the combined weight in the checklist. Mix with sugar, then vegetable oil, then sifted flour and baking powder until smooth.

steps.title: Prepare pan
steps.text: Remove kneading blade. Add batter and fit pan.

steps.title: Start
steps.text: Select program 29 and press Start.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: At completion beeps press Cancel. Remove hot pan with dry oven mitts; cool about 2 minutes then remove gently. Check for blade. Vigorous shaking can damage shape. If batter sticks to a bamboo skewer, up to two additional baking cycles, 1–30 minutes each, are available for about 15 minutes after completion before interior cools. Select program 29, set time, press Start.

otherTime: See documented method; hands-on preparation time is unspecified.

ingredients.quantity: 300 g before draining; use 160 g drained

steps.title: Prepare before starting
steps.text: Read the recipe notes. Measure all ingredients and keep any reserved ingredients separate. Do not use the delay timer.

steps.title: Dissolve gelatin
steps.text: Put 30 g water and 3 g gelatin in a heatproof container. Microwave uncovered at 700 W for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Mix and chill
steps.text: Mix milk jam, drained yogurt and gelatin mixture. Refrigerate for 1–2 hours until set.

steps.title: Prepare fruit sauce
steps.text: Put the frozen blueberries, lemon juice and granulated sugar in a heatproof bowl. Microwave uncovered at 700 W for 2 minutes. Stir and microwave another minute.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon the set dessert into dishes and pour the fruit sauce over it.

otherTime: Drain yogurt overnight; chill dessert 1–2 hr.

Program 31: Milk jam
Crème d’Anjou-style dessert

Ingredients
804kcal

Plain unsweetened yogurt
(drained) ... 160g
Water ... 30g(mL)
Gelatin ... 3g
<A>

Frozen blueberries ... 50g
Lemon juice ... 7.5g
Granulated sugar ... 25g

① Drain 300 g plain yogurt in the refrigerator overnight
until reduced to about half its weight (160 g).
② Put the water and gelatin in a heatproof container.
Microwave uncovered at 700 W for 30 seconds.
③ Mix the milk jam, drained yogurt and gelatin
mixture. Refrigerate for 1–2 hours until set.
④ Put A in a heatproof bowl and microwave
uncovered at 700 W for 2 minutes.

⑥ Spoon mixture ③ into dishes and pour ④ over it.

steps.title: Remove dough and make sauce
steps.text: At completion press Cancel and remove the dough immediately. For the sauce, combine rice flour, soy milk, bouillon and salt in a saucepan. Heat over medium heat for 2 minutes, stirring occasionally. When bubbling, reduce to low and cook for 2 minutes. Remove when thickened.

steps.title: Shape and top
steps.text: Divide into two, round, cover and rest 10–20 minutes. Roll on baking parchment to about 25 cm circles and prick with a fork. Spread the prepared white sauce and arrange the listed toppings.

steps.title: Bake separately
steps.text: Bake in a preheated oven at 180–200°C for about 15 minutes. Refrigerate waiting dough to prevent overproving.

notes: At 25°C or above use water at about 5°C (manual d5).

steps.title: Check conditions
steps.text: At room temperatures of 25°C or above, use cold water at about 5°C (instruction manual).

steps.title: Prepare and start dough
steps.text: Fit the kneading blade. Add only initial bread-pan ingredients, excluding fillings and finishing ingredients. Put dry yeast in the dry yeast dispenser. Fit the pan and close the lids. Press Dough to select d1, then Start. At completion beeps press Cancel and remove dough immediately.

steps.title: Shape and prove
steps.text: Degas from centre outwards, fold into thirds, round and put in a bowl. Prove at 25–30°C for about 30 minutes. Degas and round taut, then rest at 25–30°C for 30 minutes without drying. steps.title: Finish cooking

steps.text: Fit the kneading blade. Add only initial bread-pan ingredients, excluding fillings and finishing ingredients. Put dry yeast in the dry yeast dispenser. Add initial dry ingredients first, then yogurt, then milk. Fit the pan and close the lids. Press Dough to select d3, then Start. At completion beeps press Cancel and remove dough immediately.

steps.title: Shape and prove
steps.text: Divide into 10 pieces about 50 g; round, cover and rest 10 minutes. Arrange, slash tops and mist. Prove at 30–35°C for 40–60 minutes until doubled.

steps.title: Finish cooking
steps.text: Brush egg wash and bake in a preheated oven at 180–200°C for about 15 minutes.

otherTime: See documented method; hands-on preparation time is unspecified.

Method

1
Make enriched dough using dough program d3 (see manual).
① Fit the bread blade in the pan and add A, then the plain yogurt,
then the milk. Put the dry yeast in the yeast dispenser and make
the dough.

2
Shape
① Remove the dough and divide with a
scraper into 10 pieces of about 50 g.
Round with the smooth surface outwards,
cover with a cloth and rest for 10 minutes.
② Arrange the pieces, slash the tops and
mist with water.
③ Prove at 30–35°C for 40–60 minutes,
until about twice the size.

3
Bake
① Brush with egg wash and bake in
a preheated oven at 180–200°C for
about 15 minutes.

ingredients.name: Butter for laminating (cut into 1 cm- thick slices)

steps.title: Prepare and start dough
steps.text: Fit the kneading blade. Add only initial bread-pan ingredients, excluding fillings and finishing ingredients. Put dry yeast in the dry yeast dispenser. Fit the pan and close the lids. Press Dough to select d3, then Start. At completion beeps press Cancel and remove dough immediately.

steps.title: Shape and prove
steps.text: Refrigerate covered dough 30–60 minutes (longer in warm room). Flour the laminating butter, wrap and roll to a 20 cm square; refrigerate 15–30 minutes. Tap dough and roll to 30 cm square. Enclose butter, wrap and chill 10–20 minutes. Tap and roll flat, fold into thirds, wrap and chill 10–20 minutes. Repeat rolling and folding twice more, then chill 30–60 minutes. Divide into two; roll each to 18 × 40 cm and cut six triangles. Roll while pulling ends, place seam-down, mist, cover and prove at room temperature 40–60 minutes until doubled.

steps.title: Finish cooking
steps.text: Brush egg wash and bake in a preheated oven at 200–220°C for about 10 minutes. Refrigerate waiting dough.

A

Dough d4: Natural yeast dough

• With natural yeast
204 kcal each

A

Prepared natural yeast starter: 25 g(2
large spoons)
Bread flour: 230 g
Cake flour: 50 g
Butter: 15 g
Sugar: 25.5 g(3 large spoons)
Skim milk powder: 6 g(1 large spoon)
Salt: 5 g(1 small spoon)
Egg (beaten): 25 g(½ medium egg)
Water: 120 g(mL)

Butter for laminating (cut into 1
cm-thick slices): 140 g

To finish
Egg wash (beaten egg): 25 g (½ medium egg)

Method

1
Make the dough
With dry yeast: make enriched dough using dough program d3 (see manual).
① Fit the bread blade in the pan and add A. Put the dry yeast in the yeast
dispenser and make the dough.
With natural yeast: make natural yeast bread dough using dough program d4 (see
manual).
① Fit the bread blade in the pan and add the prepared starter, then A. Make the
dough.

2
Laminate with butter
① Remove the dough, place in a bowl, cover with cling film and refrigerate
for 30–60 minutes (longer in a warm room).
② Dust the laminating butter with flour, arrange the slices together, wrap in
cling film and roll into a square about 20 × 20 cm. Refrigerate for 15–30
minutes.
③ Press the dough with tapping motions of the rolling pin, then roll into a
square about 30 × 30 cm.
④ Place the butter from ② on the dough and enclose it. Wrap in cling film
and refrigerate for 10–20 minutes.
⑤ Tap with the rolling pin and, once slightly thinner, roll flat.
⑥ Fold into thirds, wrap in cling film and refrigerate for 10–20 minutes.
⑦ Repeat ⑤ and ⑥ twice more, then chill for 30–60 minutes.

3
Shape
① Divide into 2 with a scraper. Roll each piece into a rectangle about 18 ×
40 cm and cut into 6 isosceles triangles.
② Roll up while pulling the ends.
③ Arrange seam-side down.
④ Mist with water, cover with cling film and prove at room temperature for
40–60 minutes, until about twice the size.

4
Bake
① Brush with egg wash and bake in a preheated oven at 200–220°C for
about 10 minutes. Refrigerate the remaining dough to prevent
overproving.

name: Chocolate Cornets

steps.title: Check conditions
steps.text: Adjust ingredient temperatures so the dough is about 26°C after kneading.

steps.title: Prepare custard separately
steps.text: Whisk yolks, beat in sugar until pale, lightly mix in sifted cake flour and gradually add lukewarm milk. Strain into a saucepan. Dough d3: Rich dough
Chocolate Cornets

① Put the egg yolks in a bowl and whisk. Add the
sugar and beat until pale.
② Lightly mix in the sifted cake flour. Gradually add

③ Strain into a saucepan.
④ Heat, stirring constantly with a wooden spatula to
prevent scorching.
⑤ When glossy and falling in a stream from the

handle.

name: Melon Buns

steps.title: Check conditions

steps.title: Make cookie dough ahead
steps.text: Cream room-temperature butter. Beat in sugar in 2–3 batches until pale and smooth. Beat in egg in 3–4 batches; add optional flavouring to taste. Fold in sifted cake flour until no dry flour remains. Flatten in a plastic bag; refrigerate at least 20 minutes. Remove about 30 minutes before use to soften; divide into 8 and round.

steps.title: Prepare and start dough
steps.text: Fit the kneading blade. Add only initial bread-pan ingredients, excluding fillings and finishing ingredients. Put dry yeast in the dry yeast dispenser. Fit the pan and close the lids. Press Dough to select d3, then Start. At completion beeps press Cancel and remove dough immediately.

steps.text: Degas, divide into 8, round and rest about 15 minutes without drying. Degas and round taut, pinching bottoms. Flatten cookie pieces slightly larger than dough and cover each top. Coat cookie surface with granulated sugar and mark grid. Prove at 30–35°C for 40–50 minutes until doubled; allow surface to dry slightly.

steps.title: Finish cooking
steps.text: Bake in a preheated oven at 170–190°C about 10 minutes.

Melon Buns

Ingredients (makes 8) 331 kcal each

① Beat the room-temperature butter with a wooden
spatula or similar until creamy.
② Add the sugar in 2–3 batches, beating each time
until pale and smooth.
③ Add the egg gradually in 3–4 batches, beating after
each addition. Add any flavouring after the egg.
④ Add the sifted cake flour and gently fold with a
cutting motion until no dry flour remains.
⑤ Once the dough comes together, place in a plastic
bag, flatten and refrigerate for at least 20 minutes.
⑥ Remove about 30 minutes before use and let soften
at room temperature.
⑦ Divide into 8 pieces and round each one.

Making the cookie dough
See the variation recipes in the
instruction manual.

Method

Make enriched dough using dough program
d3 (see manual).
① Fit the bread blade in the pan and add A.
Put the dry yeast in the yeast dispenser
and make the dough.
• When the beeper sounds, press Cancel.

1

Shape
① Remove the dough, press gently to
expel the gas, divide into 8 with a scraper,
round with the smooth surface outwards
and rest at room temperature for about 15
minutes. Do not let it dry out.
② Press all over with your palm to expel
the gas. Round into taut balls with a smooth
surface and pinch the bottoms closed.
③ Flatten each piece of cookie dough into
a circle slightly larger than the bread dough.
④ Place it over the bread dough to cover
the top completely, then shape.
⑤ Coat the cookie-dough surface with
granulated sugar and mark a grid with the
scraper.
⑥ Prove at 30–35°C for 40–50 minutes,
until about twice the original size.
• Allow the surface to become slightly dry
while proving.

2

Bake
① Bake in a preheated oven at 170–
190°C for about 10 minutes.

3

name: Pizza

steps.title: Prepare and weigh
steps.text: Fit the kneading blade in the bread pan. Weigh the dough ingredients exactly. At room temperatures of 25°C or above, use cold water (about 5°C). Keep pizza sauce, cheese and toppings reserved for later. [Instruction Manual pp.18, 76; Recipe Book p.36]

steps.title: Load the bread pan and yeast dispenser
steps.text: Put flour and the other dough ingredients, except dry yeast, in a mound at the centre of the bread pan. Pour water around the edges. Fit and lock the pan in the appliance. Put dry yeast in the dry yeast dispenser. Close both lids. [Instruction Manual pp.18, 76]

steps.title: Select dough program d5 and start
steps.text: Use Dough to select d5, then press Start on the bread maker. Confirm here only after you have performed this machine action. The dough cycle is approximately 45 minutes. [Instruction Manual p.76]

steps.title: Respond to the machine’s completion beeps
steps.text: Wait for the bread maker’s beeps. Press Cancel on the machine and remove the dough immediately; it will continue to rise if left in the pan. This website does not detect the beeps. [Instruction Manual p.76]

steps.title: Divide and rest
steps.text: Divide into 2 with a dough scraper and round with the smooth surface outwards. For thinner pizza bases, the recipe permits dividing into 3. Cover with a cloth and rest for 10–20 minutes. [Recipe Book p.36]

steps.title: Shape and top
steps.text: Place on baking parchment and roll into circles about 25 cm across. Prick with a fork. Spread with pizza sauce, arrange the suggested toppings and add the pizza cheese. [Recipe Book p.36]

steps.title: Bake in your oven
steps.text: Bake in a preheated oven at 180–200°C for about 15 minutes. Refrigerate the remaining dough to prevent overproving. Follow your oven’s operating instructions. Confirm completion yourself. [Recipe Book pp.22, 36]

steps.title: Finish and clean
steps.text: After use, unplug the bread maker and allow it to cool before cleaning. Wash the bread pan and kneading blade as directed; do not immerse the appliance body. [Instruction Manual pp.5, 86–87]

notes: The machine makes the dough only. Shaping, resting, topping and baking in a separate oven are required.
The listed toppings are the source’s suggested toppings, not invented substitutions.
The optional three-base division is documented; ingredient quantities remain unchanged.
Machine actions and completion must be confirmed by you.
otherTime: Rest 10–20 min; external oven bake about 15 min at 180–200°C. Hands-on preparation time unspecified.

steps.title: Set up manual controls
steps.text: Use Stage to select Knead, Rise (called Ferment in parts of the recipe book), or Bake. Use Level and the time buttons for each setting, then Start. At each completed stage press Cancel before setting the next stage. Run the listed kneading stages separately; do not combine them into a My Knead pattern. Yeast is not dispensed automatically in manual mode: put it directly in the pan at the specified stage. Always pause with Start before inspecting dough; maximum pause is 15 minutes. A means only the initial dough ingredients; B and reserved ingredients are added when the method says.

steps.title: Make the dough and give it the first prove
steps.text: ① Fit the bread blade in the pan and add A in the listed order. ② Initial kneading: [Knead: 1] 2 min → [Knead: 3] 2 min → [Knead: 4] 10 min (14 min total). ③ Add the butter and knead again: [Knead: 2] 2 min → [Knead: 3] 2 min → [Knead: 4] 8 min (12 min total). ④ Prove at [Ferment: 3] for about 50 minutes, until about twice the original size. Remove the dough and take out the bread blade.

steps.title: Second prove
steps.text: ① Press gently to expel the gas, fold into thirds both horizontally and vertically, gather together and return to the bread pan. ② Prove at [Ferment: 3] for about 20 minutes, then remove from the pan.

steps.title: Third prove
steps.text: ① Round the dough into a ball with a taut surface. ② Prove at [Ferment: 3] for about 20 minutes, then remove from the pan.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: ① Gradually expel the gas with a rolling pin while rolling into an approximately 18 × 18 cm square. With the smooth side down, fold in one third, turn, and fold in one third again. ② Turn 90 degrees and roll from the far edge towards you, keeping the surface taut. Seal the seam firmly. ③ Return to the pan seam-side down and prove at [Ferment: 4] for 40–60 minutes, until the highest point is about 2 cm above the pan.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: ① Bake at [Bake: 2] for 35 minutes.

steps.title: Remove the bread
steps.text: At completion press Cancel. Remove the hot pan with dry oven mitts, let it cool about 2 minutes, then remove the loaf.

notes: Adjust ingredient temperatures to aim for dough at about 26°C after kneading.
Check dough condition as well as time. The source permits shorter proving in warm rooms and longer in cold rooms. Follow your oven and tin instructions.

steps.title: Prepare custard and cool
steps.text: 1 Heat the milk in a saucepan until just below boiling. 2 Whisk the egg yolks in a bowl. Add the sugar and whisk until pale. 3 Lightly mix in the cake flour. Gradually add the hot milk to loosen the mixture. 4 Strain back into the saucepan. 5 Cook over medium heat, stirring continuously with a wooden spoon to prevent scorching. 6 When glossy and loose enough to drip from the spoon, remove from the heat and add the vanilla essence. 7 Spread in a tray, cover with cling film to prevent the surface drying, and cool.

Mini Chocolate Rolls

Ingredients (about 24 rolls)
76 kcal each

Shape
1 Remove the dough from the pan. On a generously floured
board, roll into a rectangle about 40 × 20 cm.
2 Fold the long dimension into thirds. Rest at room temperature
for about 20 minutes; do not let it dry out.
3 Cut in half with a dough scraper. Roll each half into a rectangle
about 25 cm long × 15 cm wide, then cut each in half across the
width.
4 Arrange the chocolate in two slightly spaced rows on each
piece. Roll up from a long edge and place seam-side down.
5 Cut each roll into 6 with a dough scraper (24 pieces total).
6 Prove at 30-35°C for 40-60 minutes, until about 1.5 times the
original size.

Method

Make the dough and give it its first rise
1 Fit the bread blade in the pan and add A.
2 Initial kneading: [Knead 2] 2 min → [Knead 3] 2 min →
[Knead 4] 10 min (14 min total).
3 Add the butter. Knead again: [Knead 3] 2 min → [Knead
4] 8 min (10 min total).
4 [Rise 3]: about 60 min, until about 2.5 times its original
size.

Bake
1 Brush with beaten egg and sprinkle with flaked almonds.
2 Bake in a preheated oven at 170-190°C for about 8
minutes.

Bread Tart Shells

Method

Make the dough and give it its first rise
1 Fit the bread blade in the pan and add A.
2 Initial kneading: [Knead 2] 2 min → [Knead 3] 4 min (6 min total).
3 Add the butter. Knead again: [Knead 3] 6 min → [Knead 4] 5 min
(11 min total).
4 [Rise 3]: about 60 min, until about twice its original size.

Shape
1 Remove the dough from the pan and press gently to release the gas.
Divide into 10 with a dough scraper. Round each piece to give it a
smooth, taut surface. Rest at room temperature for about 15 minutes; do
not let it dry out.
2 Roll each piece into a circle about 13 cm across.
3 Cut out a circle with an approximately 11 cm round cutter.
4 Take the outer ring, stretch it thinner, twist into a figure of eight and fold
into a double ring. Set it around the cut-out circle to form a shallow dish.
5 Prove at 30-35°C for 20-40 minutes, until about 1.5 times the original
size.

3 Bake
1 Brush with beaten egg.
2 Prick the base in several places with a fork.
3 Bake in a preheated oven at 170-190°C for about 10
minutes. Cool, then top with fruit, whipped cream or similar.
• Custard and similar fillings may be added before baking.

spoons)

Egg (beaten): 25 g(½ medium egg)
Water: 140 g(mL)
Dry yeast: 2.1 g(¾ small spoons)

After initial kneading
Butter: 25 g

To finish
Egg wash (beaten egg): as
needed
Decoration
Cream (whipped with sugar): as
needed
Fruit of your choice: as needed

kneading.

ingredients to suit your taste.

steps.text: Whisk 1 g yeast into the 100 g poolish water. Mix in the 100 g poolish French bread flour until smooth with no dry flour; aim for about 25°C finished poolish. Cover, rest at room temperature about 60 minutes, then refrigerate at 3–5°C for 8–18 hours. Add this poolish with the separate main-dough ingredients A.

steps.text: 1 Fit the bread blade in the pan. Add A and the poolish, and make the dough. [Knead 1] 2 min → [Knead 3] 3 min → [Knead 4] 12 min (17 min total). 2 Remove the dough from the pan. Form a smooth, taut ball and put in a lightly oiled bowl. 3 Let rise at about 30°C for about 60 minutes.

1 Remove the dough from the bowl and divide into 2 with a dough scraper. Round loaf: round into a smooth, taut ball. Long loaf: fold from the far edge towards you to form a log about 10 cm long, with a smooth, taut surface.

• Do not round too tightly. 2 Rest at 25-30°C for about 20 minutes; do not let the dough dry out. 3 Use plenty of dusting flour when shaping. Round loaf: 1) Press all over with your palm to release the gas. Round into a smooth, taut ball, pinching the bottom closed. 2) Coat the top with French bread flour and place flour-side down in a cloth-lined rattan basket. Long loaf: 1) Press all over with your palm to release the gas. Place smooth-side down, fold in the far third and press together. 2) Turn 180 degrees, fold in the far third again and press together. Fold in half and press firmly along the edge to seal (about 16 cm long). 3) Coat the surface with flour. Lay a cloth on the board and form pleats; place the dough seam-side up between them. 4 Prove at 30-35°C. Round loaf: about 60 min. Long loaf: about 60 min.

Spray with water. 4 Bake using your oven’s automatic French bread program (about 30 minutes). To set the temperature manually: 1 Preheat the oven and tray to about 200°C. steps.title: Cream the mixture
steps.text: Beat the room-temperature butter and sugar with a hand mixer to incorporate air. When pale, add egg yolk and salt and beat until the mixture no longer drips from the whisk. Add this mixture to the initial pan with A; keep frying oil and coating sugar separate.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: ① Fit the kneading blade. Put A and the creamed mixture in the bread pan. ② [Knead 1] 2 minutes → [Knead 3] 3 minutes → [Knead 4] 15 minutes (20 minutes total). ③ Remove, shape into a taut ball and place in an oiled bowl. Prove at 25–30°C for about 50 minutes. Do not let it dry out.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text:
④ Remove from the bowl onto a canvas cloth. Roll into an 18 × 18 cm square, 1.5 cm thick. Cover with plastic wrap and rest at room temperature for 5–10 minutes. Do not let it dry out. ⑤ Cut out rings using 8 cm and 3 cm cutters. ⑥ Prove at 30–35°C for about 35 minutes. (Use the scraps for Berliner Krapfen.)

• Mist with water or use steam to prevent drying.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: ⑦ Fry in oil at 170–180°C for 1–1½ minutes on each side. Drain and cool, then coat with vanilla sugar or other toppings.

Huajuan (Flower Rolls)

Method

Shape
① Remove the dough, press out the gas
lightly and round. Rest at room
temperature for about 15 minutes.
② Roll out to 25 cm long × 32 cm wide.
Brush with sesame oil, roll up and seal.
③ Cut into 8 pieces, each 4 cm wide.
Press a chopstick firmly down the centre.
④ Place on parchment paper and leave at
room temperature for 30–50 minutes, until
1.5 times the original size.

Make the dough
① Fit the kneading blade and put A in
the bread pan.
② [Knead 2] 2 minutes → [Knead 3] 2
minutes → [Knead 4] 13 minutes (17
minutes total).
③ [Rise 3] for about 60 minutes, until
doubled in size.

Steam
⑤ Heat water in a steamer. When
steaming, arrange the dough with its
parchment paper inside. Steam over
medium-low heat for about 10 minutes.

Ingredients (makes 8)
154 kcal(per piece)

Bread flour: 50 g
Cake flour: 200 g
Baking powder: 5 g
Shortening: 10 g
Sugar: 25.5 g(3 large spoons)
Salt*: 2.5 g(½ small spoons)
Water: 130 g(mL)
Dry yeast: 2.8 g(1 small spoons)
White sesame oil: as needed

• Adjust ingredient temperatures so the dough is
about 28°C after kneading.

* You may reduce the salt to taste.

name: Pitta Bread

steps.title: Set up manual controls
steps.text: Use Stage to select Knead, Rise (called Ferment in parts of the recipe book), or Bake. Use Level and the time buttons for each setting, then Start. At each completed stage press Cancel before setting the next stage. Run the listed kneading stages separately; do not combine them into a My Knead pattern. Yeast is not dispensed automatically in manual mode: put it directly in the pan at the specified stage. Always pause with Start before inspecting dough; maximum pause is 15 minutes. A means only the initial dough ingredients; B and reserved ingredients are added when the method says.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: ① Fit the kneading blade and add all the ingredients. [Knead 2] 1 minute → [Knead 3] 3 minutes → [Knead 4] 12 minutes (16 minutes total). ② [Rise 3] for about 45 minutes, until doubled in size.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: ③ Remove the dough, press out the gas and divide into 6. Shape into smooth balls and rest at room temperature for about 10 minutes. ④ Dust with flour and roll into even rounds about 3 mm thick.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: ⑤ Preheat the baking tray in the oven. Bake at 190–210°C for about 8 minutes, until puffed up like balloons.

notes: Check dough condition as well as time. The source permits shorter proving in warm rooms and longer in cold rooms. Follow your oven and tin instructions.

steps.title: Check conditions before preparing
steps.text: The machine delay timer is unavailable for this program (manual pp. 8–11, 24).

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Fit kneading blade. Add egg-and-milk mixture, then yogurt, then remaining ingredients. Fit pan. At 15°C or below cut butter into 5 mm cubes.

steps.title: Start
steps.text: Select program 25 and press Start.

steps.title: Scrape flour at machine beep
steps.text: Open lid and scrape flour from sides using a rubber spatula; metal damages coating. Do not press Cancel. Within 3 minutes close lid and press Start again.

steps.title: Shape at next machine beep
steps.text: After about 1 minute(s), open lid, scrape dough from sides and shape into a dome. Do not press Cancel. Within 3 minutes close lid and press Start again.

steps.title: Finish and check
steps.text: At completion beeps press Cancel. Remove hot pan with dry oven mitts; cool about 2 minutes then remove gently. Check for blade. Vigorous shaking can damage shape. If underbaked, up to two additional baking cycles are available for about 15 minutes after completion, before interior cools. Select same program, set 1–20 minutes, press Start. If Cancel has not been pressed, set time then Start. Hold Cancel to stop.

notes: Use high-protein Japanese bread flour with at least 11% protein. Results vary by brand, variety and harvest year. The source accepts a baked height of at least 10 cm (7 cm for quick bread).
First scraping beep after about 2 minutes.
If 3 minutes elapse at scraping, the program resumes automatically.
If Cancel is pressed accidentally at an intervention, press Start within 10 minutes to resume (once only; pressing another key disables this).
The program resumes baking automatically after 3 minutes at the shaping step. Wipe oil fumes from lid and steam vent after use (pp. 86–87).
The machine delay timer is unavailable for this program (manual pp. 8–11, 24).

ingredients.name: Butter for laminating (cut into 1 cm-thick slices)

steps.title: Prepare starter and dough
steps.text: Use prepared natural yeast starter (manual p. 45). Stir before measuring. Fit the kneading blade, add the starter first, then the remaining initial dough ingredients. Keep laminating butter and egg wash separate. Fit pan, close lid and select Dough d4, then Start. At completion press Cancel and remove dough immediately.

steps.title: Shape and prove
steps.text: Refrigerate covered dough 30–60 minutes (longer in warm room). Flour the laminating butter, wrap and roll to a 20 cm square; refrigerate 15–30 minutes. Tap dough and roll to 30 cm square. Enclose butter, wrap and chill 10–20 minutes. Tap and roll flat, fold into thirds, wrap and chill 10–20 minutes. Repeat rolling and folding twice more, then chill 30–60 minutes. Divide into two; roll each to 18 × 40 cm and cut six triangles. Roll while pulling ends, place seam-down, mist, cover and prove at room temperature 40–60 minutes until doubled.

steps.title: Finish cooking
steps.text: Brush egg wash and bake in a preheated oven at 200–220°C for about 10 minutes. Refrigerate waiting dough.

notes: Prepare starter using program 23 (24 hours) in advance; stir before measuring. At 25°C or above use cold water about 5°C.

• With natural yeast
204 kcal each

A

Prepared natural yeast starter: 25 g(2
large spoons)
Bread flour: 230 g
Cake flour: 50 g
Butter: 15 g

Skim milk powder: 6 g(1 large spoon)

Egg (beaten): 25 g(½ medium egg)
Water: 120 g(mL)

Butter for laminating (cut into 1
cm-thick slices): 140 g

To finish
Egg wash (beaten egg): 25 g (½ medium egg)

Method

1
Make the dough
With dry yeast: make enriched dough using dough program d3 (see manual).
① Fit the bread blade in the pan and add A. Put the dry yeast in the yeast
dispenser and make the dough.
With natural yeast: make natural yeast bread dough using dough program d4 (see
manual).
① Fit the bread blade in the pan and add the prepared starter, then A. Make the
dough.

2
Laminate with butter
① Remove the dough, place in a bowl, cover with cling film and refrigerate
for 30–60 minutes (longer in a warm room).
② Dust the laminating butter with flour, arrange the slices together, wrap in
cling film and roll into a square about 20 × 20 cm. Refrigerate for 15–30
minutes.
③ Press the dough with tapping motions of the rolling pin, then roll into a
square about 30 × 30 cm.
④ Place the butter from ② on the dough and enclose it. Wrap in cling film
and refrigerate for 10–20 minutes.
⑤ Tap with the rolling pin and, once slightly thinner, roll flat.
⑥ Fold into thirds, wrap in cling film and refrigerate for 10–20 minutes.
⑦ Repeat ⑤ and ⑥ twice more, then chill for 30–60 minutes.

3
Shape
① Divide into 2 with a scraper. Roll each piece into a rectangle about 18 ×
40 cm and cut into 6 isosceles triangles.
② Roll up while pulling the ends.
③ Arrange seam-side down.
④ Mist with water, cover with cling film and prove at room temperature for
40–60 minutes, until about twice the size.

4
Bake
① Brush with egg wash and bake in a preheated oven at 200–220°C for
about 10 minutes. Refrigerate the remaining dough to prevent
overproving.
